q: Are iron ore pellets and iron ore fines covered by EU CBAM?
title: Are iron ore pellets covered by CBAM?
short: Pellets are covered, fines and lump ore are not. Agglomerated iron ores and concentrates, which include pellets and sinter, fall under CN 2601 12 00, which is listed in Annex I of the CBAM Regulation. Non-agglomerated iron ore, such as fines and lumps under 2601 11, is not covered.
audience: Pellet plants and iron ore exporters in Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka and Goa

ul: 2601 12 00, agglomerated iron ores and concentrates, other than roasted iron pyrites: covered. This includes pellets and sinter.
2601 11, non-agglomerated iron ores and concentrates, such as fines, lumps and beneficiated concentrate: not covered.

p: CBAM counts the direct emissions of making the pellets: fuel burnt in the induration furnace or travelling grate, such as coal, coke breeze, furnace oil or gas, and process CO2 from carbonate additives like limestone and dolomite. Electricity for grinding and balling is not counted for iron and steel goods in the definitive period.

Pellets are often a precursor for DRI and blast furnace iron. If you also make sponge iron or pig iron from your own pellets and export those, the pellets' embedded emissions are carried into the downstream product's figure, so the same data serves twice.

ol: Calendar-year fuel and additive consumption for the pellet plant.
Pellet production and moisture basis, so the importer can work per dry tonne if asked.
Carbon content of coal, coke breeze or other fuels from supplier analyses.

p: Under the 2025 simplification, an EU importer bringing in less than 50 tonnes a year of covered goods is exempt. Pellet cargoes are far larger, so in practice every pellet importer is in scope.
